title: Exploratory Synthetic Studies of the Praseodymium/Di-2-Pyridyl Ketoxime System Leads to Unusual Reactivity and Interesting New Molecules

material_class.structural_family: dinuclear Pr(III) complex with two head-to-head 2.2011110 L− bridges

synthesis.procedure: Method A (aerobic): solid dpkoxH (0.080 g, 0.40 mmol) was added to a stirred pale green solution of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (0.174 g, 0.40 mmol) in MeCN (25 mL). The green solution was stirred 30 min, filtered, and stored at room temperature. Pale green X-ray quality crystals of 1·3MeCN formed over 6 weeks, were collected, washed with cold MeCN (2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 3 mL), and dried in a vacuum desiccator over silica gel. Method B: to a pale green solution of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (0.435 g, 1.00 mmol) and dpkoxH (0.199 g, 1.00 mmol) in MeCN (10 mL) was added slowly Et3N (0.14 mL, 1.00 mmol) with stirring. After 30 min the solution was filtered and left in a closed flask at room temperature; crystals formed in 2 months. Dried samples analyze as lattice-solvent-free 1.

material_class.structural_family: dinuclear Pr(III) complex with two head-to-head 2.2011110 L− bridges (MeNO2 solvate of 1)

synthesis.procedure: To a pale green slurry of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (0.435 g, 1.00 mmol) in MeNO2 (10 mL) was added slowly a colorless solution of dpkoxH (0.199 g, 1.00 mmol) and Et3N (0.14 mL, 1.00 mmol) in MeNO2 (15 mL). The green suspension was stirred, filtered, and the filtrate left for slow evaporation at 5–6 °C. Pale green X-ray quality crystals formed after 2 months, were collected, washed with cold MeNO2, and dried in air. Analysis matches 2·3MeNO2.

synthesis.procedure: To a pale green solution of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (0.435 g, 1.00 mmol) and dpkoxH (0.199 g, 1.00 mmol) in MeCN (10 mL) was added slowly n-Bu4NOEt in EtOH (0.85 mL, 1.00 mmol). The green solution was stirred 30 min, filtered, and stored at room temperature. Pale green X-ray quality crystals of 3·2MeCN formed in 1 week, were collected, washed with cold EtOH (2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 3 mL), and dried in air. Dried samples analyze as lattice-MeCN-free 3.

material_class.structural_family: nonanuclear mixed-valence {Pr8IIIPrIV(μ3-O)4(μ3-OH)4} cluster described as four fused butterflies

synthesis.procedure: To a pale green solution of Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (0.217 g, 0.50 mmol) and dpkoxH (0.199 g, 1.00 mmol) in EtOH (15 mL) was added slowly Et3N (0.18 mL, 2.00 mmol). The green solution was stirred 30 min, filtered, and left undisturbed in a closed flask. After 2 days, n-hexane (2 mL) was added. Green X-ray quality crystals of 4·4EtOH·4(n-hexane) formed after 2 weeks, were collected, washed with cold EtOH (2 mL) and Et2O (2 × 3 mL), and dried in a vacuum desiccator over silica gel. Dried samples analyze as lattice-solvent-free 4.

synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic stirring, closed-flask crystallization after n-hexane addition

properties.summary: X-band EPR of powdered 4 at 4.2 K shows a sharp peak at 630 G, a derivative feature at 1340 G, and weaker additional signals, interpreted as consistent with the half-integer spin of a 4f1 Pr(IV) center.
